# Generated code

The tool emits one function: a bootstrap you register on form OnLoad, which registers everything
else at runtime. This is the whole output for a Contact form carrying one of each supported
event kind:

```javascript
// Generated by Events2Code (XrmToolBox) on 2026-08-17
// Entity: contact   Form: Contact
// Register ONLY this function on the form OnLoad event (pass execution context).
"use strict";

var MyOrg = MyOrg || {};
MyOrg.FormEvents = MyOrg.FormEvents || {};

MyOrg.FormEvents.onLoad = function (executionContext) {
    var formContext = executionContext.getFormContext();

    // --- Form OnSave ---
    formContext.data.entity.addOnSave(MyOrg.Contact.onSave);

    // --- Attribute OnChange ---
    formContext.getAttribute("parentcustomerid")?.addOnChange(function (executionContext) { MyOrg.Contact.onParentCustomerChanged(executionContext, "accountid", true); });
    // (disabled in designer) formContext.getAttribute("emailaddress1")?.addOnChange(function (executionContext) { MyOrg.Contact.validateEmail(); });

    // --- Tab state change ---
    formContext.ui.tabs.get("tab_details")?.addTabStateChange(MyOrg.Contact.onDetailsTabToggled);

    // --- Subgrid OnLoad (grid controls may not exist yet at form OnLoad) ---
    formContext.getControl("Cases")?.addOnLoad(MyOrg.Contact.onCasesGridLoad);

    // --- Original form OnLoad handlers ---
    MyOrg.Contact.onLoad(executionContext);
};

// NOT converted - left registered on the form:
//   setadditionalparams general -> AppCommon.Contact.Instance.parentCustomerOnChange (AppCommon/Contact/Contact_Main_Library.js) [internal handler, owned by Dynamics]
```

## Event mapping

| Designer registration | Generated call |
|---|---|
| Form OnSave | `formContext.data.entity.addOnSave(handler)` |
| Attribute OnChange | `formContext.getAttribute("name")?.addOnChange(handler)` |
| Tab state change | `formContext.ui.tabs.get("name")?.addTabStateChange(handler)` |
| Subgrid OnLoad | `formContext.getControl("name")?.addOnLoad(handler)` |
| Form OnLoad | called directly from the bootstrap |

Form OnLoad has no `addOnLoad` on the form itself, so the original OnLoad handlers are simply
invoked in the bootstrap body — which runs at OnLoad. That also means exactly one designer
registration survives the migration: the bootstrap.

## Conventions the output follows

**Namespaces are declared.** `MyOrg.FormEvents.onLoad` produces `var MyOrg = MyOrg || {};` and
`MyOrg.FormEvents = MyOrg.FormEvents || {};` before the assignment, so the file is safe to load
in any order relative to your other scripts.

**Optional chaining guards every lookup.** A field, tab, or grid that is missing from the form
variant being loaded returns `null`; without `?.` the registration would throw and every
registration after it would never run. This makes the output ES2020 — fine for Unified
Interface, but check any minifier or ESLint config pinned to ES5.

**Execution context and extra parameters are preserved.** How the handler is passed depends on
what the designer recorded:

| Designer settings | Generated handler argument |
|---|---|
| Pass execution context, no parameters | `MyOrg.fn` — passed straight through |
| Anything else | `function (executionContext) { MyOrg.fn(/* recorded args */); }` |

The wrapper exists because the Client API only ever hands a handler the execution context. Extra
parameters recorded in the designer are re-emitted verbatim in the same order the platform would
have passed them: execution context first when the flag is set, then the parameter list.

**Disabled handlers are emitted commented out.** They stay visible — with a
`// (disabled in designer)` prefix — so nothing quietly disappears in the migration, but they
stay switched off. Uncheck them in the grid to leave them registered on the form instead.

**Anything not converted is listed at the bottom.** Each skipped handler is written out as a
comment with the reason, so the generated file is a complete record of what the form had.

## What you do with it

The tool does not create or upload the web resource — it prints the code and, on request, saves
it to a file. Put that code in the web resource you named, publish it, and only then
[unregister](form-changes.md). Nothing about the generated code depends on the file name; the
name matters only because the form has to load the library that contains the bootstrap.
